name: abstinence
description: The voluntary act of avoiding a behavior that may have brought pleasure or relief.
perceptions: There's something specific that I should not experience at this time.
It's not healthy for my body or my spirit.
results: Each instance of abstinence may be easy or a very difficult act of willpower.

guidance.description: If you need help abstaining from something addictive, consider finding a support group or professional help.
For general tips, see guidance on 'willpower'.

variations.name: hesitant abstinence
variations.description: The internal conflict of wanting to avoid something while also partly wanting to indulge in it.
perceptions: Someone or something is tempting me away from a goal of avoiding something.
Avoiding this thing is pretty important to me.
But the downside of not doing it also feels significant.

variations.name: satisfied abstinence
variations.description: A gentle sense of pride for successfully living up to the goal of avoiding something that may have brought pleasure or relief.
perceptions: Someone or something tempted me away from the goal of avoiding something.
But avoiding the thing is very important to me.
I was successfully avoided it.

variations.name: frugality
variations.description: The habitual practice of avoiding unnecessary material and experience-based luxuries, and being efficient with given resources.
perceptions: I'm happy with the things and experiences I have.
I don't need a new thing or experience.
It would be improper for me to indulge in unnecessary luxuries.
I should not get used to having nice things.
I prefer to manage my resources efficiently.
examples: Limiting how much you spend on entertainment.

variations.name: abstaining from small talk
variations.description: The habitual practice of avoiding unnecessary social communication.
perceptions: I'm confident in myself.
I don't need to engage in meaningless social contact.
I recognize there is sometimes social pressure to reaffirm relationships.
I'll reserve my communication for meaningful things.
People who engage in small talk are shallow.
results: You may gain a reputation as a serious person or as a distant/aloof person.

guidance.description: There are several reasons people refrain from social pleasantries. Maybe it feels boring. Maybe there's a self-image involved. Maybe there's anxiety about making a verbal mistake. Here are some references.
Tips on focusing your conversations on things that matter.

variations.name: chastity
variations.description: The habitual practice of avoiding unnecessary sexual contact.
perceptions: I'm saving myself for the right person and right time.
Sexual contact has several potentially serious implications.
results: You may gain a reputation as a wholesome person or a prude.

variations.name: temperance
variations.description: The habitual practice of strictly controlling your engagement in unnecessary pleasures.
perceptions: I believe that indulging in pleasures is unhealthy in the long run.
I prefer to moderate my participation in certain pleasurable activities.
results: You may gain a reputation as a wholesome person or a prude.

comparisons.description: 'Abstinence' is a absolute. 'Temperance' is moderate abstinence, where an occasional indulgence is allowed.

examples: Drinking alcohol only on special occasions.
Allowing yourself dessert only once a week.

comparisons.description: 'Frugality' and 'chastity' are specific forms of abstinence.

commentaries.quote: Complete abstinence is easier than perfect moderation.
I pass the test. I will diminish, and go into the West, and remain Galadriel.
commentaries.attribution: J.R.R. Tolkien in Fellowship of the Ring

commentaries.quote: Never go to excess, but let moderation be your guide.
Too many people spend money they haven't earned to buy things they don't want to impress people they don't like.
Chastity is the cement of civilization and progress.
Silence is a source of great strength.
